recommendations.rationale: Terminal reach passes while sampled holding position and speed fail; the candidate causes are not separated and key records (per-update horizons, saved projected states, full plans) are unread or not retained. Defer any weight change until a bounded comparison is authorized and the missing records are read.

Recorded terminal_tip_speed_weight is 0.0 and holding-window tip speed remains far above the 0.02 m/s settling limit, making a positive tip-speed weight a testable candidate under the later control grant. No winning value is justified by these selected-row records, so no value is proposed here.

attribution.reason: Recorded terminal_tip_speed_weight is 0.0 while tip_speed_scale_m_s is 0.02 m/s and holding-window tip speed stays 0.635-1.581 m/s against a 0.02 m/s settling speed limit. A zero recorded weight means the corresponding tip-speed penalty term is recorded as absent, which is a reasonable and testable candidate for high residual holding speed, and terminal_tip_speed_weight is one of the two weights the later control grant permits changing. Raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance, so this is a candidate, not an established cause.

34 of 35 stopping counts are User_Requested_Stop with only one Solve_Succeeded, returns are labelled budget_best_feasible or relative_seed_improvement, and displayed projection_residual_rad_m is about 2.4-2.9 rad/m at the final updates. This is consistent with accepted-but-early-stopped plans being executed during the holding window; the retained records do not include the selected cost or the optimizer traces needed to show that the accepted plans failed to regulate speed.

Recorded mean_update_s 17.26331904856488 s and update_wall_s up to 18.444833799963817 s greatly exceed control_period_s 0.01 s, and deadline_misses equals update_count. Whether these synchronous wall overruns changed the executed simulated trajectory (skipped, delayed or stale control intervals) is not established by these records; the inventory explicitly lacks closed-loop counterfactual replay.

Aligned first-step comparisons show close tip agreement (for example 0.001183439178222365 m tip difference at update 34) while projection_residual_rad_m is about 2.4-2.9 rad/m. A single-step projected-model probe cannot account for a sustained holding-window speed failure; the retained records do not separate model error from controller stopping behaviour.

The effective_horizon values decline with the final updates (6 at update 29, 4 at 31, 2 at 33) while the sampled record ends at 0.35 s with terminal_speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 m/s, i.e. the tip is still moving when the record and holding window end. The retained records cannot show whether the shortened lookahead or the short remaining episode duration limits braking; no trajectory extension or counterfactual replay is available.

For every displayed update plan_accepted is true, solver statuses recorded are User_Requested_Stop (34) and Solve_Succeeded (1) with no solver_failed indication, and returned/selected constraint violations in the displayed final updates are small (about 1e-8 to 4e-4). This rules out a missing-plan failure for the displayed updates; it is not established for the updates whose solver records were not displayed.

recommended_actions: Before any parameter change, read the unread per-update effective_horizon records (source.controller_horizon for updates 0-16 and 18-27) and saved projected states (source.saved_projected_states) to test whether holding speed was represented during the approach.
Treat terminal reach and sampled holding as separate criteria: the terminal reach pass is one endpoint sample and does not evidence settling.
If a bounded comparison is later authorized, restrict it to the permitted weights (terminal_tip_speed_weight, holding_tip_speed_weight); do not change geometry or material.
